title: red faction
text: Red Faction, I always thought of it as a fantastic game, a game of mystery and adventure. I originally bought the game back in 2001 thinking that it would be a simple escape from the grind of life. A game to quickly play, beat, and then likely forget about after finishing it like so many other shooters at the time. Man, was I a fool. Playing the game was a blast, I never gave myself a free moment from the day I first booted it up. Until the Mass Effect series concluded, Red Faction was ranked my most favorite game of all time. I picked it up again on Steam a while back and even though it had been so long since I had played it before, I was right back into it, I felt like the first time I picked it up. Sure the graphics aged, and technically a lot about the game was a relic to what we have nowadays, but it still had that charm which I fell in love with so many years ago. Few games to me have held up over the years as well as this has. It's not for everyone, but it is for me, and that's what counts! 9.5/10 still in my eyes!

text: My rating in short: go to bottom line. Only reason why I got this game was because the 4- part series was worth $11. Being the chonologically obsessive guy I am, I had to start rom the beginning. I was surprised that this game was originally released in the first month or so of the PS2's release. I was even more surprised on how absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game was.  The overall story is pretty simple. It's your basic FPS with a variety of weapons killing the same guards over and over as you try to escape Mars from the oppressive mining organization Ultor. Later, you realize Ultor has been experimenting on the miners for some undisclosed reason. Must be a new evil pasttime. As soon as you dispatch the evil cyborg scientist, who evidently is also a magic user somehow, you continue your quest. However, then you have mercenaries drop in on you, along with their ruthless commander, who ALSO has unexplained magic powers. Graphics seem like they belong in the old Quake games, characters forgetable, and the voice acting is laughable. Gameplay is as simple as it gets; go from point A to point B while shooting down anyone and anything within sight. I do applaud the little bits that break the linear paths. Every so often, there's an alternate path in which you can traverse, and end up completely skipping a wave of enemies you'd normally face if you went the obvious route. The biggest problem I had was the enemy AI. At the beginning, the evil guards are laughable, the way they seem to dance all over the place and shout at you in a very cartoonish manner. "Miner scum!" "Where do you think YOU'RE going, miner trash?". For those who enjoy sneaking behind a group of enemies and catching them unawares will be repeatedly disappointed, as the enemy seems to have eyes in the back of their head. And as soon as ONE guard notices you, everyone and their mother unloades on you. It gets even more difficult in the second half of the game when the guards take many more shots (and multiple headshots) to kill, and your still as weak as ever. These armored up baddies also can blast you with one-shot killing rail guns, which they tend to fire just as soon as you pass around the corner. Sometimes, they don't even have to see you; their rail gun shots go through walls. Many rage moments were had. This game has so many glitches in it that I could go on and on about all of which that I've encountered...but I think you get the overall message. Don't. Just don't.

text: Definitely a great throwback FPS; if you find it on sale, go get it. The story is so outrageous, you can really see Volition's knack for crazyness here. Besides the outrageousness that it shares with Saints Row, it also shares the same Ultor Corporation (and thus is set in the same universe). Gameplay is definitely fantastic, they just don't make games like this anymore. There a difficulty curve about halfway through the game (right when you unlock the Precision Rifle) where you just get bombarded with enemies that are accurate and health drops become less common, so be warned if you aren't used to older FPS games and game mechanics. The story on normal takes about 9 hrs to complete, and there is multiplayer, although outside of the RF hardcore, I doubt there's many people still playing (last I heard, around 9-16 people still play). TL;DR go pick it up for a decently fun and cheesy campaign, as well as stellar FPS gameplay.

text: I had no non-COD FPS experience before I played this game, so it was quite a learning curve. Unless you're used to ARMA 2 or a game like that, prepare to die, and die, and die some more. Be pleased if you don't finish a game at the very bottom of a server. But it is worth it. It sounds great, it feels great, and the fact that you have a lot of Russian players shouting at you over the voice chat somehow enhances the realism! BUT: Since the release of RO2, the number of people on RO2 servers has fallen dramatically, at peak time there will be a full Panzer server (where the players are impossible to beat imho!) and maybe a couple of infantry servers, but this'll continue to fall. The game offers a single player vs AI training mode, which is useful to learn about the maps but the bots themselves are appallingly useless. The realism of this game is great though, only in ARMA 2 have I been more afraid of dying! It is very exciting to play, and can involve some great teamwork: You spawn, you run to the nearest half-track, joining your comrades in the back you speed through the fields towards the front. Artillery rains down around you. An enemy tank is seen in the distance and fires. Bailing out the smoking vehicle, you dive into the hedge. Crawling along this, you meet a support trench that takes you closer to the action. Bullets zip above your head. Where are they coming from? You wriggle up to a fellow machine-gunner, and resupply him with ammunition. Whilst he changes the smoking barrel, you fire off a few rounds with your semi-automatic rifle to keep their heads down. More friendly riflemen join you. Fixing your bayonet, you leap out of the trench and sprint towards the nearest building. A bullet catches you in your hand, causing you to drop your rifle, leaving you defenceless. You pause momentarily, and an enemy sniper hits you. Cue shot of your body falling to the ground. Repeat x many. But was it fun? YES

text: First off, I can't believe this game is free!!! I would've bought this gem up for a good amount! Well hopefully it'll stay that way for a little while at least. ANYways, this game is fantastic in pretty much every aspect. The art is cutesy and at the same time rough and tumble, it reminds me a little of the Power Puff Girls and that's definitely a compliment. The colors are bright and punchy and I think that adds to the high energy experience. The music is catchy and fun, it definitely adds a lot to the feel of the game and it gets your blood up for some rootin' tootin' shootin'. The gameplay itself is pretty dang solid, aiming and shooting is really fun and easily controllable, and I absolutely LOVE the way the grenades work, they are fun to chuck about, but of course they're limited so it adds that level of decision making to the game, you have to decide if the situation really requires one or not. The only thing I would say needed improvement is the character selection. Now to be clear, I love the available characters I've played so far, but it would be nice to have some more diversity and some cool new faces to choose from. (Or maybe even a character creator, just a thought.) Also, maybe a couple more starting characters to choose from and some more that don't require as many achievments to play with as a little added bonus for beginners. That said, this game is definitely worth the price and then some! If they charged $15 for this i wouldn't even bat an eye, it's THAT good. 10/10 much good game

title: remember me
text: Absolutely recommend this game, if its on sale, be sure to pick it up. PROS: -Interesting, unique story -Interesting distopian future -Beautifull overall theme and style of Neo-Paris and graphics look really good -Combat system, unlocking awesome moves throughout the game and freedom to choose how you fight + combo system is a lot of fun to play with -Freerunning and climbing almost has a little Assassins creed feeling to it# -Freedom to explore some areas to find bonuses CONS: -Fighting, especialy boss battles get repetitive and a bit boring + enemies have repetitive attack paterns and always appear waves in certain areas, not randomly throughout the world -Some of the puzzles with memory remixing are very difficult or far-fetched (or I am just very stupid) -game is scripted, you run allong a set story, there is no choices and the story feels a bit forced at some moments Conclusion: interesting game that is a lot of fun to play around with. The game looks beautifull and it perfectly sets a very interesting theme for a distopian future that I have not seen before. IF you're looking to have some fun, an interesting story that you dont mind # its scripted and a game that you can finish about 20h, be sure to pick up this game when its on sale

title: remember me
text: Fellow gamers! Why did we up vote this game enough for it to have very positive reviews? For those considering to buy this game, do not waste your money unless it's on sale for $5 or less. Let's start with the good. Game have some fluid combat, easy combo system to get into. Climbing and jumping is nice and easily handled. Main character is very nice to look at, custom is design was nice touch. Upgrading is simple and sticks to the game plan and looking for hidden items really does count considering nothing else will give you more health. Now the bad. Story doesn't make sense. Period. Japanese manga does have history to go far off when it comes to story telling but they do it in artistic style. This game on the other hand, does not. Everyone have memory weakness sticking out back of their neck. No cover or nothing to hide it. While at times people have to use a professional equipment to remove memory from person, at other times you can do it not even touching the victim. Story goes one way than it goes the other. It could had been one of finest story, yet Capcom went and messed it up. Camara is alot of time your #1 enemy. The bosses are a joke and only thing it really is your last OMG push this button fast! type of fight.
